chapter: Nancy Wilson, Wes Montgomery and Joe Williams
title: Building a buzz for Nancy; the later split caused by her husband
summary: Nancy became his main focus, with demand created before her recordings, though her husband later sidelined the partnership for a time.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: I guess you could say now that you created a buzz about her. You just . . .
You build up some – there was a lot of talk about her before she . . .
Before she ever hit the set. That’s true.
But there was a period also when you broke with her for a little while.

That’s much longer down the line. It’s much further down the line. That’s after her [being] established at the Coconut Grove, to be a big star, go to Las Vegas, and doing her own show. That’s much later – three, four years later.
So at that period, she was the main person you were working with. Who else was coming on board.

I still had my staff of people that I was working with and had people – Chuck Taylor was still working with me, working with people. I still was managing people and handling other things. She was just a main – she became the main purpose of my thing, because I could foresee in Nancy – she had all the qualities of being a class act, where she could do movies. I pictured all that, and to some degree she did do it, but we got sidelined four or five years into her career by her husband. That has happened to a lot of artists. That changed things around for a while. We had to start all over again four years later.
